Original analysis retained for provenance: The advisory and reporter reproduction match the source lifecycle: an authenticated editor supplies an SVG, unvalidated client code persists it in public object storage as a course cover, and opening that stored resource executes SVG script. History following is essential here: 804e5cdeb980f83e37d5d688a00d4a6b61e690a1 merely centralized already-vulnerable upload logic, and b0da3099f8f3fd4934bbea0dba84edaa043b1a74 added a later landing-page route; neither is the BIC. The earliest preserved origin aggregate 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e adds the flawed course-cover uploader and its direct parent lacks those lines, and it predates every tagged 0.1.x release including 0.1.13. However, its own commit message proves it squashes numerous original changes, and the recorded MR/member history is unavailable. Under the protocol a squash aggregate is not a BIC, so its human-looking commit-object metadata cannot support NOT_AI and no AI verdict can be made from another commit. The later fix and release boundary are closed: 900f5ec12979f512ae8f333312aee78973a054f5 introduces the SVG-excluding allowlist and is exactly release v0.2.5, after vulnerable v0.2.4.
